 We are looking for a highly motivated Research Fellow to work on novel technologies and applications of fibre communication systems.

 Be a part of the University of Southampton, an institution in the top one per cent of world universities and one of the UK’s Russell group research-intensive universities. We have an international reputation for research, teaching and enterprise activities. You will work in the world leading Optoelectronics Research Centre (ORC) and will have access to the world class facilities and dedicated researchers that this provides. The Telecommunications Systems Laboratory is equipped with state-of-the-art equipment for experimentation in photonic systems and provides direct access to the UK’s National Dark Fibre Facility, a unique geographically distributed transmission facility dedicated to research, linking together four top British universities.

 You will contribute to research projects that experimentally investigate communication systems using state-of-the-art optical technologies, including novel amplifiers, integrated photonic components, and hollow-core and multi-core optical fibres. Your research will explore the potential of these technologies in future communication systems. This will require an in-depth understanding of the physical characteristics of optical fibres and devices, and the ability to develop innovative ways to deploy them in network configurations. You will work closely with project partners and other researchers within the group and across the ORC.

 To be successful, you must have a strong background in photonics and communications with extensive practical experience of working with optical fibres and systems. Ideally, you will also have experience in characterising optical fibres, photonic components, optical system modelling and/or the design and experimentation of high-speed optical communication systems.

 You must also have proven skills in the critical evaluation and interpretation of data, reporting your findings succinctly and working as part of a collaborative research team. You must hold a PhD* or equivalent qualification related to fibre optics or photonics. Previous postdoctoral experience is favoured but not necessary.

 If you have any questions or would like to discuss this post, please contact Professor Periklis Petropoulos on pp@orc.soton.ac.uk .

 This is a fixed-term position at 0.8FTE (28 hours per week) until 31 st March 2027.   

 LSE’s awarding winning R&I Evidence and Analysis Service is seeking to appoint a Research Officer to work on the UKRI/DSIT funded project ‘What is unique about responsive mode funding?’ The project is a collaboration between research management professionals based at LSE and computer scientists at the University of Edinburgh. It will investigate historic UKRI administrative data to better understand the role of responsive mode funding within the wider UK R&I ecosystem.  

 The role will involve analysing administrative data and developing (with computer science colleagues) visualisations and written outputs which provide new insights into responsive mode funding programmes. The research will seek to understand the impact of responsive mode funding on areas such as research trends, levels of interdisciplinarity, cross-sector collaboration, policy engagement and knowledge transfer. The post will sit in the R&I Evidence and Analysis team within the Research and Innovation Division. There will be opportunities to interact with LSE’s world-class social science researchers via the project steering group as well as opportunities to establish interdisciplinary collaborations with project team members working in high-performance computing at the University of Edinburgh.  

 The postholder will have a PhD, be working towards completion of a PhD, or have other research experience that demonstrates the capability to produce independent original research. They will also have experience working with large administrative datasets and will be expected to have a strong understanding of the UK research and innovation policy and funding landscape. 

 This is a fixed-term position at 0.8FTE (28 hours per week) for 10 months.

 Postdoctoral research scientist at the University of Reading in probabilistic storylines of climate extremes   

 A postdoctoral research scientist post is available to develop a novel statistical approach to frame extreme event storylines in likelihood space, using conditional probabilities to distinguish between dynamical and thermodynamic effects. Professor Fowler will also co-supervise the post-holder. The University of Reading is a world-leading centre for meteorology and climate, with a large and vibrant community of early-career researchers, and with the ECMWF moving onto campus in 2027.

 A PhD or equivalent in meteorology or a related field 

 A proven track record in research, demonstrated through excellent peer-reviewed publications 

 Proficiency in atmospheric data analysis 

 Good written and communication skills 

 Capability of independent thought 

 Knowledge of multivariate statistical modelling, atmospheric dynamics, extreme weather events, climate variability and change, and weather and climate modelling  

 Knowledge of one or more of machine learning, causal effect networks, and climate storylines is desirable but not essential.

Research Assistant – Real World Evidence

Job id: 162885. Salary: £41,445 per annum inclusive of London Weighting Allowance.

Posted: 09 November 2026. Closing date: 22 November 2026.

Business unit: Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine. Department: Comprehensive Cancer Centre.

Contact details: Mieke Van Hemelrijck. Mieke.vanhemelrijck@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Guy's Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About Us

The TOUR (Transforming cancer OUtcomes through Research) team at King’s College London brings together researchers, clinicians and other healthcare professionals to improve cancer outcomes through patient-centred research and the effective use of clinical and real-world data. The multidisciplinary team, led by Mieke Van Hemelrijck, works closely with colleagues across Guy’s Cancer and the wider cancer research community.  

A major focus of our work is the Guy’s Cancer Real World Evidence (RWE) Programme, jointly led by Mieke Van Hemelrijck and Anne Rigg. The programme aims to strengthen real-world evidence and data science capability within Guy’s Cancer, enabling high-quality, patient-centred research that addresses important questions about cancer care and outcomes.

The RWE programme brings together researchers, clinicians and other collaborators around a growing portfolio of research projects and data initiatives. The successful applicant will join this collaborative environment and help ensure that projects, research applications, data requests and data-sharing activities are coordinated effectively across the programme.

TOUR is based within the Centre for Cancer Society and Public Health at King’s College London, providing a wider multidisciplinary research environment spanning cancer prevention, early diagnosis, treatment and care, patient experience, inequalities and cancer outcomes. 

About The Role

This is an opportunity to join the TOUR team and support the coordination and delivery of the Guy’s Cancer Real World Evidence (RWE) Programme. The programme brings together researchers, clinicians, data specialists and other collaborators to enable high-quality research using real-world cancer data.

The post holder will play a central role in coordinating the RWE research portfolio, supporting projects from initial enquiry and research application through data access, approvals, delivery and reporting. You will help maintain oversight of multiple projects and data requests, coordinate meetings and actions, support research applications and data-sharing processes, and ensure effective communication between the different stakeholders involved.

You will work closely with academic and clinical colleagues, research and data teams, and internal and external collaborators. An important part of the role will be acting as a point of coordination for researchers wishing to work with the RWE programme, ensuring that requests are progressed efficiently and that project documentation, decisions, timelines and outstanding actions are appropriately tracked.

The role will also contribute to the management and development of RWE databases and research resources and to the wider operational organisation of the TOUR RWE programme.

This is a full time post (35 Hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

Bachelor’s degree in a health, biomedical, population health, data science or other relevant discipline.
Knowledge of clinical and/or health research processes, including research governance, data protection and GDPR requirements.
Excellent organisational and project management skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple research projects, maintain accurate records, monitor timelines and follow up actions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, including researchers, clinicians, data teams and external collaborators.
Experience of supporting the preparation and coordination of research applications, project documentation, approvals or related research administration.
Ability to coordinate data access and data-sharing activities, including managing data requests, tracking approvals and liaising with relevant stakeholders to support timely progression of requests.
Ability to prioritise competing demands, work independently, use initiative and proactively identify and resolve operational issues.
Strong IT and information-management skills, including confidence using Microsoft Office applications and maintaining project trackers, databases and shared documentation.

Desirable criteria

Experience of coordinating research projects within a university, NHS, healthcare or cancer research environment.
Experience of working with real-world health data, clinical datasets, research databases or data-access processes.
Experience of supporting research collaborations involving multiple organisations and/or multidisciplinary stakeholders.
Experience of research governance processes, including ethics, R&D approvals, data-sharing agreements, data-access requests or related documentation.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the next page after you click “Apply Now”. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

Further Information

We pride ourselves on being inclusive and welcoming. We embrace diversity and want everyone to feel that they belong and are connected to others in our community.

We are committed to working with our staff and unions on these and other issues, to continue to support our people and to develop a diverse and inclusive culture at King's.
We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the advert. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Job Title:  Research Associate in Computational Pathology and Multimodal AI
Posting Start Date:  09/11/2026

Work Arrangement:  Full Time (On site)

Salary per annum (£):  £39,560 - £48,337

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

 

We are looking for a Research Associate to join the NEOPATH research group in the School of Clinical Dentistry, University of Sheffield. You will develop and validate deep learning methods that combine routine histology with radiology, multiplex imaging, spatial transcriptomics and clinical data to predict how oral and head and neck cancers behave and how they respond to treatment.

The group is led by Professor Ali Khurram, a Professor and consultant in oral and head and neck pathology. The group’s work includes multicentre validated tools for detecting and grading oral epithelial dysplasia, and profiling tumour infiltrating lymphocytes in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Current programmes, funded by Cancer Research UK, Stand Up To Cancer and MRC, address cancer risk in oral potentially malignant disorders, and response to treatment.

Your research will centre on building and training models on large whole slide image, radiological and genomic cohorts for a range of cancer, linking image features to clinical outcomes and testing whether those models hold up on data from other centres and scanners. Alongside this, you will coordinate team meetings, work with our academic, clinical and patient collaborators, help develop grant applications and papers, and present our work at scientific and public events.

The post would suit someone with a PhD in a computational or quantitative field, or someone from a pathology or biomedical background who has built substantial programming and machine learning skills. A background in histopathology, radiology, omics and bio-informatics is a clear advantage, because much of the work sits where pathology and computation meet. We will provide clinical training for strong candidates from a computational background.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

Design, train and validate deep learning models for diagnosis, grading and outcome prediction in cancer.

Develop multimodal models that integrate histology with radiology, multiplex immunofluorescence or immunohistochemistry, spatial transcriptomics and clinical variables.

Build and maintain reproducible pipelines for slide preprocessing, stain normalisation, tissue and cell segmentation, feature extraction and model evaluation, using version control and clear documentation.

Curate and manage large imaging and clinical datasets in line with ethics approvals, data protection law and NHS information governance requirements.

Carry out external validation across centres and scanners, and assess model calibration, bias and failure modes.

Bring histopathological and computational thinking together, working with pathologists to design annotation protocols, check that model outputs make morphological sense and interpret explainability analyses.

Support the principal investigator in the day to day coordination of the group, including organising team meetings, tracking milestones and keeping work aligned across projects.

Act as a regular point of contact for academic, clinical and patient collaborators, and help sustain these working relationships.

Contribute to the supervision and support of postgraduate students working on related projects.

Contribute to grant and fellowship applications, including preliminary data, methods and supporting documents, and help identify suitable funding opportunities.

Lead and contribute to manuscripts, technical reports, and code and data releases.

Present the group's work at national and international conferences, seminars, and patient and public engagement events.

Keep up to date with the literature in computational pathology and medical AI, and bring relevant new methods into the group.

Follow University policies on health and safety, data protection, research integrity and sustainability.

Carry out other duties as required, commensurate with the scope and grade of the post.

Person Specification 

Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. About the role

Are you a talented cell and developmental biologist ready to work at the interface of biology and microelectronics? As a Research Associate in Brain Organoids and Organ-on-Chip Platforms, you will lead the biological arm of a new programme combining semiconductor-based lab-on-chip technology with human brain organoids.

You will bring the biological expertise that our engineering team needs, and in return gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge chip technology, co-author high-impact interdisciplinary papers, and help shape the direction of a growing research area. Within two years, you will deliver validated brain-organoid protocols and device-compatible culture methods for our semiconductor platforms.

The group of Prof. Pantelis Georgiou develops lab-on-chip systems based on semiconductor technology. We design, fabricate and test integrated sensing and microfluidic platforms built on CMOS technology, taking ideas from concept through to working devices for biological applications, clinical validation and translation. We are now extending this work to complex three-dimensional human brain organoid models, in collaboration with colleagues in Medicine. Imperial offers an outstanding environment for this work, with access to world-class cleanroom, imaging and bioengineering facilities and a strong community in engineering, neuroscience and stem cell biology.

What you would be doing

You will establish and characterise robust brain organoid culture in our laboratory and work alongside engineers and device physicists to integrate organoids onto chip platforms, creating organ-on-chip systems that enable sensing, stimulation and monitoring of organoids.

You will be responsible for:

Generating and maintaining brain organoids (for example cortical or region-specific organoids) from human pluripotent stem cells, with reproducible quality control
Characterising organoids using immunostaining, imaging, gene expression and functional assays
Working with engineers to design biocompatible chip interfaces, culture conditions and protocols for long-term organoid culture on devices
Testing and validating device performance with living tissue, and feeding results back to the design cycle
Analysing and interpreting data, and writing papers, reports and conference presentations
Helping train and supervise PhD and MSc students in cell culture and biological methods
Contributing to grant applications and collaborations

What we are looking for

You will hold (or be about to obtain) a PhD in a relevant discipline such as stem cell biology, neuroscience, developmental biology, tissue engineering or a related field.

You will have demonstrable hands-on experience of culturing human pluripotent stem cells and generating 3D neural models, and you will be keen to work in a multidisciplinary team with engineers. You do not need a background in electronics or microfabrication; we will teach you what you need, however prior experience with commercial MEA platforms may be useful.

You will be an excellent communicator, with the ability to manage work to deadlines.

What we can offer you

An exciting opportunity to develop a new programme at the interface of biology and microelectronics, working with a welcoming multidisciplinary team, state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technologies.

 

As a member of Imperial research staff, you will have the opportunity to:

continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity,
grow your career with access to Imperial’s dedicated career support for researchers, plus opportunities for promotion and progression,
develop your skills and explore your career prospects with 10 development days per year,
benefit from a sector-leading salary and remuneration package,
be part of a diverse, inclusive and collaborative work culture with various staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing.

 

 

Further information

Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant.

 

Please include in your application a CV with publication list and cover letter (maximum two pages) describing your experience with organoids and your interest in working with engineering platforms.

 

If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Prof Pantelis Georgiou (pantelis@imperial.ac.uk)

About us 

We are a vibrant, diverse Department that looks to lead innovation in education and research at one of the world’s leading universities. To support our ambition, King’s has invested in new multi-million-pound teaching and research laboratories of more than 3000 sqm for the Department at heart of its Strand campus, which opened in August 2022. We celebrate diversity and actively promote an inclusive environment and encourage applicants from underrepresented groups. In moving our ambitions forward, we are continuing to appoint academics to join us in shaping the future of education and research for King’s Engineering. We offer undergraduate and postgraduate education, with a distinctive approach, combining traditional teaching methods with modern, project-based learning, catering for the needs of our students and the industries in which they will work.  It is essential that applicants have the enthusiasm and commitment needed to ensure the success of these programmes.

About the role 

We are seeking an enthusiastic and committed academic to contribute to the design, delivery, and continuous enhancement of teaching within our Engineering programmes. The primary purpose of this role is to deliver high-quality, research-informed education that equips students with both strong theoretical foundations and practical, industry-relevant skills, particularly in mechanics, materials, design, mathematics & computing.

The postholder will take responsibility for leading and contributing to a range of modules across the undergraduate curriculum. This includes supporting Year 1 and 2 Engineering through tutorials and hands-on laboratory teaching. These roles involve designing and delivering lectures, workshops, and project-based learning activities, as well as overseeing assessment and ensuring alignment with learning outcomes and current industry practice.

The role holder will be responsible to the relevant Programme and Department leadership and will work collaboratively with academic colleagues, technical staff, and professional services teams to ensure the effective delivery of modules and a high-quality student experience. They will also contribute to educational development by engaging in evidence-based teaching practice, driving innovation in pedagogy, and responding to student feedback through active engagement with student representatives.

In addition, the postholder will support outreach and widening participation activities, representing the department at events such as open days. They will also contribute to the administrative processes associated with teaching and assessment, ensuring smooth module operation and compliance with institutional requirements.

This is a full time post (35 hours per week), and you will be offered 1-year contract until 31 August 2027.

About you

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria 

MEng qualified in Engineering or a closely related discipline
Ability to deliver and assess technical and practical teaching in areas such as electrical and electronic engineering 
Experience and knowledge of project-based learning and group supervision in engineering or computing disciplines
Ability to design and deliver engaging, inclusive teaching at undergraduate and/or postgraduate level
Experience in marking of coursework and/or examinations at levels 4-7 and providing high quality feedback to students
Interest in pedagogic innovation, curriculum development and enhancement of student experience through research-informed best practice in engineering education
Commitment to an inclusive learning and working environment working with a range of students and role-holders

Desirable criteria

Eligibility for, or awarded, associate fellowship of the Higher Education Academy (AHEA)
Evidence of educational innovation including development of new tools, resources and methodologies
Evidence of excellent student or peer feedback on teaching and learning
Experience delivering STEM outreach or widening participation activities

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. Fixed Term End Date: 31 March 2030

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Tuesday 5 January 2027, 11:59 PM (UK)                        

Full time Salary Range: £50,000 - £60,000 (specific salary as per Marie Curie funding rate). This includes a mobility allowance.

About the Role

 

Applications are invited for two 36-month positions as Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Candidates (DC1 and DC2) in the areas of synthetic organic chemistry, polymer chemistry and sustainable materials. The successful applicants will join the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network (DN) AGRIPOLYS, working under the supervision of Prof. Remzi Becer at the University of Warwick

.

AGRIPOLYS is funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Programme under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement number 101311807. The network brings together fifteen doctoral projects on the molecular design of polymers for sustainable agriculture, with a focus on biodegradable seed coatings and agrochemical carriers that replace persistent plastic-based materials. The Doctoral Candidates will be trained in the design, synthesis and characterisation of these polymers, their formulation and application, and the evaluation of their biodegradation and environmental fate.

 

Further information is available at https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311807/en

 

Eligibility: at the time of recruitment, researchers must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the United Kingdom for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to the appointment date. At the time of recruitment, the applicant must not yet have been awarded a doctoral degree. The posts are open to applicants of any nationality, subject to the mobility rule above.

 

For candidates whose first language is not English, an IELTS (or equivalent) score of at least 6.5 is required. Applicants who do not hold a valid English certificate at the time of application must give a clear plan, with dates, for obtaining one.

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

About You

 

These Doctoral Candidates positions are offered in conjunction with PhD studentships at the University of Warwick, subject to the applicants satisfying the University’s admissions requirements. The successful applicants will be required to enrol for a PhD degree under the supervision of Prof. Remzi Becer.

 

DC1: Synthesis of functional polymers for reducing dust-off on seed coatings. The DC will synthesise poly(2-oxazoline)s of different architecture and composition and relate polymer structure to film formation on seeds and to the reduction of friction and dust. Secondments will take place at ETH Zurich (tribology of seed coating polymers) and Bayer Crop Science (performance testing of seed coating formulations, including dust-off and flowability).

 

DC2: Synthesis of biodegradable poly(2-oxazoline)/polyphosphoester copolymers for agricultural applications. The DC will develop copolymers that combine biodegradability with the release of fertilising degradation products, and will determine their biodegradation and fragmentation profiles to identify microplastic-free compositions. Secondments will take place at the University of Twente (design of phospholane-based monomers) and Covestro (scale-up of poly(2-oxazoline)/polyphosphoester synthesis).

 

We are looking for a polymer chemist with very good training in organic chemistry, who is interested in sustainable materials and who enjoys working across disciplines and sectors in a supportive, international team. You will be trained by an internationally recognised team of academic and industrial experts. Applicants with different backgrounds and career paths, including career breaks, are very welcome, and you do not need to meet every desirable criterion to apply.

 

Please note that we are unable to respond to enquiries, or accept CVs or applications, from recruitment agencies.

About the Department

 

The Department of Chemistry at Warwick is a thriving and inclusive community of students, academics, researchers, and professional services staff.

Our fundamental research pushes boundaries across all major fields of chemistry, while our applied work - delivered through close partnership with the wider scientific community and industry - addresses major global challenges, breakthroughs in health, solar energy harvesting, and sustainable materials.

We are proudly outward-facing, and our community is recognised as one of the strongest in the UK. Our extensive national and international relationships create an outstanding environment for collaboration, innovation, and career development. From polymers and catalysts to computation, advanced instrumentation and cutting-edge materials, our research sits at the forefront of the discipline.

We are highly interdisciplinary, having long-standing partnerships with the School of Life Sciences, Warwick Medical School, Physics, Manufacturing, Computer Science, Engineering, and Mathematics.

We are committed to fostering a supportive and inclusive working and learning environment in which diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are recognised, respected, and valued. Our Athena Swan Silver Award reflects our ongoing efforts to embed equality, diversity, and inclusion into our culture, practices, teaching, and research, and our commitment to supporting the career progression of all staff.

Explore our webpages to learn more about the Department of Chemistry’s research and teaching, industry-leading facilities, and the impact of our work.

How to Apply

 

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter on the closing date stated.

 

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications

We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. About the role

The European eel is critically endangered, and generating new understandings on its continental life stages is crucial to the recovery of populations. As Postdoctoral Research Assistant on the externally funded CRISIS project, you will lead research uncovering the ecology and demography of glass eels and elvers in rivers across southwest England.

You will lead fieldwork and laboratory research investigating eel dispersal, trophic ecology, age and growth, and parasitology. Using otolith microstructure, you will assess age and growth rates, while stable isotope analysis will help reveal the trophic relationships and movements of glass eels and elvers entering these rivers. The role also offers opportunities to support project delivery, coordinating research and project management tasks with internal colleagues and external partners.

You will hold a PhD (or be close to completion) in fish ecology, aquatic biology or a closely related discipline. You will be capable of completing fieldwork in lowland rivers and upper estuaries, and detailed laboratory analyses, ideally with experience in otolith microstructure and stable isotope methods, and hold a driving licence. A strong publication record appropriate to your career stage is advantageous, alongside excellent organisational skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

The Centre for Human & Applied Physiological Sciences (CHAPS) is situated within the School of Basic & Medical Biosciences(within the Faculty of Life Sciences and Medicine), which is led by Professor Mathias Gautel and comprises five departments with a wide range of expertise and interests.

About the Role  

About the Role

We are seeking a talented and motivated Postdoctoral Research Assistant to lead the bioinformatics framework for a high-impact project. You will analyse existing spatial transcriptomics datasets to unlock fresh insights into murine Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD). You will perform digital microdissection by manually or computationally drawing around cysts to isolate disease-specific regions and uncover localised niches of inflammation. Additionally, you will characterise complex ligand-receptor interactions, with a specific focus on dissecting the crosstalk between epithelial cells, immune cells, and fibroblasts following JAK inhibition.

About You

You must hold a PhD (or be close to completion) in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or a quantitative biological field. You must possess documented experience managing spatial/scRNA transcriptomics workflows. Strong programming proficiency in R or Python is essential. Proven experience in data acquisition, integration, deconvolution, and calculating cell-cell communication networks is highly desirable. You must be able to work independently to drive computational pipelines and communicate discoveries effectively within a multi-disciplinary translational research team.

About the School/Department/Institute/Project

The post is funded by Barts Charity and hosted within Dr Maria Fragiadaki’s laboratory at the William Harvey Research Institute (WHRI), based in the Centre for Translational Medicine and Therapeutics at the John Vane Science Centre. The successful candidate will spearhead the project: 'Dissecting the Anti-Inflammatory Impact of JAK Inhibition in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD): Using Spatial Transcriptomics to Dissect Pathophysiology.' This study utilizes cutting-edge 10x Genomics Visium spatial transcriptomics to map how a novel anti-inflammatory treatment affects disease progression. The role offers an exceptional environment to produce high-impact translational research

At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable.

Throughout our history, we’ve fostered social justice and improved lives through academic excellence. And we continue to live and breathe this spirit today, not because it’s simply ‘the right thing to do’ but for what it helps us achieve and the intellectual brilliance it delivers.

Queen Mary’s commitment to our diverse and inclusive community is embedded in our appointments processes. The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice.

LSHTM is seeking to appoint a Clinical Research Fellow - International Lead Clinician within the Department of Clinical Research. The post-holder will be responsible for the day to day running of a multi-site phase IIb into phase III randomised clinical trial of adjunctive interferon gamma for HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis in Botswana, Malawi, South Africa and Uganda. They will work closely with the experienced senior trial management team, a trial manager and study coordinators at the participating African study sites. The applicant will be expected to be based full-time at the Trial Coordinating Centre in Gaborone, Botswana for the duration of the study recruitment and travel frequently to the other sites. The applicant will have the opportunity to work in a dynamic, international and supportive research environment and to shape the conduct of this clinical trial from the outset. They will also be expected to contribute to the data analysis and any peer-reviewed publication arising from the study, and to develop and lead related sub-studies or projects.

The successful candidate will hold a medical degree (clinicians from a variety of backgrounds will be considered) with a proven experience in the conduct of clinical trials or clinical research, ideally at senior level. They will have substantial clinical experience in the management of patients with HIV infection and opportunistic infections, including experience relevant to cryptococcal meningitis and clinical and research experience in resource-constrained healthcare settings in Africa. Further particulars are available in the job description.

The post is fixed term and full-time, 40 hours per week, 1.0 FTE. The post is funded for a period of 48 months and is available from 01 January 2027. 

The salary will be in the range £47,551 to £78,898 per annum pro rata, or £67,325 to £77,348 per annum pro rata for eligible clinical academic doctors in higher specialty training (ST3 and above), depending on the applicable clinical academic salary scale and the successful candidate's circumstances. A Clinical Displacement Allowance of £2,162 per annum pro rata is payable where applicable. 

The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service. Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part-time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in Gaborone, Botswana. 

Applications should be made on-line via our jobs website. Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk. Please quote reference ITD-CRD-2026-26.

The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable.
